<!-- pr-reviewer: fa53fdf1c679ab90f76e623b3d3c7ac1fd57b613 -->
Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is the independent review. The earlier marker came from the author's own account.

What looks good
- Test-only change. Only three files in `crates/app/tests/` and one decision file change. No file under `crates/*/src` changes.
- No golden changes. No snapshot PNG changes. No dependency changes.
- The `#[test]` count rises by one in each file: `trochoid_law` 6 to 7, `circular_pick_law` 4 to 5, `circular_entity_law` 4 to 5. No test is removed. No law assertion is removed.
- The fixture fix is correct. A box stock is centered on `Location.pos`, so `pos (0, 0, 0)` puts the stock on `[-20, 20]^2 x [0, 8]`. The quarter turn keeps the footprint.
- The new pinning tests assert the stock bounds. The `job()` functions assert them too.
- A decision file is present: `docs/decisions/1608-trochoid-fixture-stock.md`. The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1608`.

Results merged with main (local, no Actions run)
- Trial merge with `origin/main`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test trochoid_law --test circular_pick_law --test circular_entity_law`: 5 passed, 5 passed, 7 passed. 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Requested before merge
- None.

Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. `crates/app/tests/trochoid_law.rs:181`: the call changes from `assert_post_refused(.., true)` to `.., rotated)`. In the aligned case, the test no longer checks that the refusal text names the operation gouge (`T1: move ... cuts past the finish surface`). The refusal itself is still asserted. The operation gouge is still asserted on the line before (`gouges(&warns) > 0`). The reason is in the new comment and in the decision file: with the full stock, the program simulator leads the message. This is a small narrowing of one check. The maintainer can accept it or ask for a check that the message contains one of the two clauses.
2. The same change applies at line 195 only if it was already `rotated`. It was. No other change there.

I did not run the full suites or the release gate. Windows-only arms are not relevant: no `cfg` lines change.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
